sections.title: The letter Ix
paragraphs: You call this letter (Ix) /ɪks/. It mainly sounds like the start of (Xylophon) /ksyloˈfoːn/, which means xylophone. This letter has two sounds in German.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, press your back tongue against the soft roof. Release the air quickly, then hiss with your tongue tip behind your upper teeth. Keep your voice off. For the second sound, make the same movements, but turn your voice on for the hissing part. Voiced means your vocal cords shake. Put your hand on your throat to feel the shake.

sections.title: When each sound occurs
paragraphs: In almost all German words and Greek loanwords, you hear the voiceless sound. You hear it in (Hexe) /ˈhɛksə/ and in (Xylophon) /ksyloˈfoːn/. Occasionally in French or English loanwords, you hear the voiced sound. You hear this in (Examen) /ɛkˈzaːmən/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: At the start of a word, do not say a single z sound like in zebra. Start with a firm k sound instead, just like in box. In loanwords, do not drop the first stop sound. Say both parts clearly.
